attributes.residual: ONE INSTRUCTION, identical mechanism to the twin. Instruction count EXACT (target 52 / ours 52); the prologue, all three `__dla__FPv` release calls, the whole zeroing block, the `bl fn_800D9CF4` call, the `__unexpected` island and the full aliased teardown (`mr r12,r31` / `lwz r0,60(r31)` / `lmw r28,40(r12)` / `lwz r1,0(r1)`) all match byte-for-byte. Only `mr r3,r28` is positioned early (end of guarded body) instead of inside the epilogue before the `lmw`. Same blocker and same next step as attempt.dtor800db21c-cpp-conversion-eh-recovered.20260831.v2: the epilogue placement requires a real C++ destructor, hence a mangled `__dt__` symbol and a class identity that is not yet established. NOTABLE SUB-FINDING, generalisable: converting the region to C++ parsing caused MWCC to auto-inline fn_800D9CF4 into this destructor (it had stayed out-of-line under the C parse), adding a 10-instruction block and pushing the body to 61 instructions -- a REGRESSION disguised inside an otherwise large structural gain. fn_800D9CF4 has exactly ONE call site (this one), so wrapping its definition in `#pragma dont_inline on/off` restored the target's `addi r3,r28,60` / `li r4,-1` / `bl` call form and took the body from 61 to exactly 52 with no effect on any other function. LESSON: after switching a region's front end, re-check inlining decisions before reading the instruction-count delta.
